newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN BUDGET REFORM FIRMS UP WITH TAX BILL.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN BUDGET REFORM FIRMS UP WITH TAX BILL.

text.p: Approval of the South African Revenue Services Bill (SARS) by the parliamentary finance committee on Tuesday is another building block in budget reform, Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said on Tuesday.

Briefing journalists after the committee approved the bill with amendments, Manuel said the reform process involved moving on to three year budgets, strengthening the department of state expenditure and beefing up tax collection.
The bill, which is due to be debated in parliament on August 19, aims to provide SARS with greater autonomy to step up tax collection.
It was supported by all parties except the Democratic Party, which felt that there should have been greater consultation on it and that it did not offer SARS enough autonomy.
Manuel said that his deputy, Gill Marcus, would meet top SARS staff at this week to discuss ensuring SARS could swing into action as soon as the bill became law, probably in early October.
The SARS board would be appointed by the end of the year.
"We want to be in the starting blocks and know exactly what the nature of the changes will be," Manuel said.
All these steps would be followed by the publication of a white paper on budget reform.
"It will be quite detailed and it will cover both the planning side and the financial management side and it will largely give effect to enormous changes which are presently underway," he said.
It had been decided to bring the white paper in only at the end of the process because it would be important first to build up capacity among staff to implement changes.
Manuel said he was particularly concerned that large corporations still had the ability to manipulate their tax returns while smaller taxpayers were paying the full tax due.
